en.p: There are two circles $C_1$, $C_2$ centered at the points $\mathrm{O_1}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$, respectively, each with radius $\overline{\mathrm{O_1O_2}}$. As shown in the figure, three distinct points A, B, C on circle $C_1$ and a point D on circle $C_2$ are given, and the three points A, $\mathrm{O_1}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$ lie on a line, as do the three points C, $\mathrm{O_2}$, D. Let $\angle\mathrm{BO_1A}=\theta_1$, $\angle\mathrm{O_2O_1C}=\theta_2$, $\angle\mathrm{O_1O_2D}=\theta_3$.

en.fig: See the original for the figure.

en.p: The following is the process of finding the ratio of the lengths of segment AB and segment CD when $\overline{\mathrm{AB}}:\overline{\mathrm{O_1D}}=1:2\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta_3=\theta_1+\theta_2$.

box: Since $\angle\mathrm{CO_2O_1}+\angle\mathrm{O_1O_2D}=\pi$, $\theta_3=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+\dfrac{\theta_2}{2}$, and from $\theta_3=\theta_1+\theta_2$ we get $2\theta_1+\theta_2=\pi$, so $\angle\mathrm{CO_1B}=\theta_1$.
Then $\angle\mathrm{O_2O_1B}=\theta_1+\theta_2=\theta_3$, so triangles $\mathrm{O_1O_2B}$ and $\mathrm{O_2O_1D}$ are congruent.

en.p: Let $f(k)$, $g(k)$ be the expressions that fit (A) and (C), respectively, and let $p$ be the number that fits (B). What is the value of $f(p)\times g(p)$? [4 points]
